source: User-requested v9 visual base, revised to the Annotation Alignment and Execution & Audit workflow. Train-only expression error analysis and whole-dataset staging audit.

updates.title: An end-to-end agent system
updates.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual. Edit the supplied v9 slide as a finished 16:9 illustration. Preserve its white background, navy typography, glossy orange robots, teal humans, purple corpus documents, blue executor chips, pastel local panels and generous spacing. No outer frame. English only. Preserve page number. No fabricated results. Keep unmentioned content unchanged. No model weight training.
Keep the v9 overview composition. Rename left heading "ANNOTATION ALIGNMENT · Steps 2–4" and right heading "EXECUTION & AUDIT · Step 5". Left stages stay Explore, Workbench review, Apply + check. Center outputs become "Approved rules + guideline" and "Versioned reference labels". Right stations become "Rewrite expression", "Run Train + Test", "Evaluate + analyze". Label the blue internal return arrow "Train errors only". Replace the large purple return caption with "Issue report: suspected label errors, rule gaps, conflicts". This return must run FROM Evaluate + analyze TO Workbench review, NOT in reverse. It is a central feature. Keep Step0, Step1 and Step6/7 scaling path. Step6 says "Freeze + release check". Bottom amber box says "New rule or label issues reopen Steps 2–4". Footer "Audit both sets. Rewrite from Train. Human decisions update rules and labels." updates.notes: The system coordinates Annotation Alignment (Steps 2–4) and Execution & Audit (Step5). The latter includes a Train-only expression refiner and an auditor that can inspect both Train and staging Test. Rule or reference-label issues from either set become reports for human adjudication through the Alignment Agent. Each round fixes compatible rule, expression and reference-label versions. Only human-approved changes reopen rules or accepted labels. Stage Test is not an end-to-end independent benchmark once its findings guide revisions. Production uses an explicitly frozen release and audit policy.

updates.title: Step 5: execute, evaluate and analyze errors
updates.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual. Edit the supplied v9 slide as a finished 16:9 illustration. Preserve its white background, navy typography, glossy orange robots, teal humans, purple corpus documents, blue executor chips, pastel local panels and generous spacing. No outer frame. English only. Preserve page number. No fabricated results. Keep unmentioned content unchanged. No model weight training.
Rework the v9 circular workflow to make its distinct operations clear, using the same art style and spacious layout. Title "Step 5: execute, evaluate and analyze errors". Subtitle "EXECUTION & AUDIT: inspect both sets, refine expression from Train".
Main four-station loop clockwise: upper-left orange robot "REWRITE EXPRESSION" / "Wording, order, examples"; upper-right blue chips "RUN LABEL EXECUTORS" / "Apply the guideline to Train + Test"; lower-right blue report "EVALUATE LABELING PERFORMANCE" / "Quality, coverage, speed and cost by set"; lower-left robot magnifier "ANALYZE ERRORS" / "Inspect cases, rules and label disagreements".
Connect rewrite→run→evaluate→analyze. The analyze→rewrite return arrow MUST be labeled "Train error analysis only". A separate teal document "REFERENCE LABELS" / "Hidden from executors" feeds ONLY Evaluate. Top small lock "Approved rules stay fixed during rewriting".
Below Analyze, show four small distinct diagnosis cards in one row: "Expression issue / Rewrite from Train", "Suspected wrong label / Human review", "Rule gap or conflict / Alignment review", "Executor limit or ambiguity / Record or defer". Do NOT draw every diagnosis directly to Rewrite. A purple outgoing arrow from the middle two cards toward lower edge is labelled "Issue report to Alignment Agent". Footer "Model disagreement is a flag for review. Model weights stay fixed." Preserve page12. Do not use phrase Score predictions. Keep short text and no tiny paragraphs.
updates.notes: Execution & Audit applies the same candidate and fixed-weight executor configuration to both Train and staging Test, then separately evaluates labeling performance and analyzes item-level failures. Quality uses task-appropriate agreement metrics against current references; coverage includes unresolved and abstained items. Runtime tools measure speed and cost. Reference labels are available to the scorer, not the target executor prompt. Auditor access to both sets does not authorize the expression refiner to read Test cases, errors, reports or memory. The refiner receives Train evidence only and preserves the current rule meaning. Diagnose expression issues, suspected wrong reference labels, rule gaps/conflicts and executor/context/ambiguity limitations. Model consensus is not ground truth. Rule and label issues route to Alignment for human decisions. The loop runs until declared criteria, diminishing gains, unresolved issues or a budget stop, producing a report even if no candidate qualifies. Report quality floors and stronger-model degradation, not gap reduction alone.

updates.notes: This synthetic Test item illustrates a suspected reference-label mismatch under a current rule. Executor disagreement is a trigger for investigation, not an authoritative correction. The reviewer should inspect original context and annotation provenance, retain the option to keep the label or defer, and explicitly distinguish label-only correction from rule change. An approved rule change triggers affected-item review; approving a rule does not approve all propagated labels. The report tracks the rule/expression/reference version and origin partition. Human review can use this staging Test case, but doing so is development exposure for subsequent claims.

noteUpdates.notes: The core unit of human work is a consequential judgment about a rule, group, contrast, exception, or conflict. The agent retrieves cases from the corpus and brings a focused question to the human. It records the answer, updates the rule and identifies affected labels. Information and rules evolve with examples rather than being completed before any labeling occurs. The human retains authority over meaning. An accepted output may be a small reviewed subset or a larger batch accepted under a stated audit policy. Unknown or deferred cases remain visible. High-level judgments can coexist with occasional item checks. Both use cases share the same scaling path. After human approval of the standard, test the same guideline across fixed executor models, refine wording without changing approved meaning, qualify an executor, and apply it to the large unlabeled corpus. Audit batches and route uncertain or conflicting cases back for review. The larger labeled corpus is not assumed to have every item manually reviewed. The three visual rows distinguish dialogue, paired accepted outputs, and execution at scale. The dialogue produces both a structured, adaptive guideline and human-approved, guideline-consistent labeled data. This accepted data may be a small reviewed subset. The two outputs remain aligned as human decisions refine the standard. Adaptive means approved meaning can evolve through human review of new evidence; executor-driven wording changes must preserve approved meaning. Both outputs support executor testing; Train case-level evidence drives expression rewriting. Staging Test is also audited and may produce issues for human Alignment review; it is not globally unseen once those findings affect revisions. The model-expanded corpus is accepted under the stated review or audit policy. In the proposed Workbench interface, the dialogue is primarily a sequence of decision reports with rule-level choices and comments. Chat is supplemental. Both channels feed the same versioned decision record.

Existing labels are evidence of prior decisions, not unquestioned ground truth. The agent infers candidate rules and constructs issue groups containing supporting items, conflicting cases, contextual differences, alternative explanations and resolution status. A flag does not establish an error. A reviewer can clarify, correct or defer, and need not be the original annotator. An audit without a reviewer may deliver provisional rules and issue groups without certifying an approved standard. Once meaning is accepted, keep the approved semantics fixed while testing wording across independent executor models. Operational release uses declared quality criteria and audit policy. Independent claims about unseen data require fresh confirmation beyond staging. This scaling stage also follows use case 1. Uniform performance across all models is a research goal, not an established result. The LEFT labeled corpus is starting evidence, not the target collection. Existing labels may reveal patterns but are not automatically gold labels. The human reviewer confirms, revises or defers candidate rules and issue groups. The RIGHT large unlabeled corpus is a distinct target for expansion and supplies new boundary cases. The shared downstream path is structured guideline, cross-model executor testing, and large-scale labeling with audit. Meaning changes require human approval; wording refinement preserves that meaning. The three visual rows distinguish dialogue, paired accepted outputs, and execution at scale. The dialogue produces both a structured, adaptive guideline and human-approved, guideline-consistent labeled data. This accepted data may be a small reviewed subset. The two outputs remain aligned as human decisions refine the standard. Adaptive means approved meaning can evolve through human review of new evidence; executor-driven wording changes must preserve approved meaning. Both outputs support executor testing; Train case-level evidence drives expression rewriting. Staging Test is also audited and may produce issues for human Alignment review; it is not globally unseen once those findings affect revisions. The model-expanded corpus is accepted under the stated review or audit policy. In the proposed Workbench interface, the dialogue is primarily a sequence of decision reports with rule-level choices and comments. Chat is supplemental. Both channels feed the same versioned decision record.

Proposed portability experiment. Hold approved information and rules fixed while comparing initial wording, refinement against a single executor, and refinement against multiple executors. Give refinement methods comparable development data and tuning budgets, and use the same facilitator capability where feasible. Recheck semantic fidelity against the approved standard. Keep development cases, calibration decisions and final evaluation cases separate. Freeze candidate wording and acceptance thresholds before the final test. Test the same guideline in fresh model contexts with fixed weights and allowed inputs only, excluding hidden facilitator conversations. Evaluate inexpensive small, intermediate and strong models, plus previously unseen executor models when feasible. Report quality with uncertainty by model and class, coverage, abstention, cost per accepted item, and human review cost. Select a quality metric suited to the task, such as macro-F1 for appropriate categorical labels, rather than assuming accuracy alone. A useful result raises the weakest required model's quality, limits deterioration of strong models within a predefined tolerance, and lowers total accepted-item cost while meeting coverage requirements. A reduced cross-model gap alone can reflect all models becoming worse. Report guideline-development cost separately and its amortization over corpus volume. If the guideline is revised after test inspection, reserve fresh evaluation cases for the new candidate. Benefits remain hypotheses. This slide describes the separate research evaluation on fresh independent cases. Its unseen evaluation set is distinct from the repeatedly audited staging Test inside Step 5. Staging results alone do not establish whole-system generalization. When reference labels change, report label corrections separately from expression-only gains.

The Agent system executes the end-to-end delivery phase: batches target items, calls qualified executors with the frozen guideline, tracks versions, routes risk cases, reconciles missing or duplicate outputs and conducts audit. Human reviews unresolved meaning and risky cases as needed; direct human review and batch acceptance have different provenance. Include random audit samples among apparently easy or agreeing cases as well as risk-stratified checks. Estimate population error with an appropriate sampling design. Repeat production batches and audits while the frozen standard and acceptance policy hold. Output includes exact guideline version, accepted labels with provenance, unresolved items and quality report. A new meaning defect reopens Steps 2-4 through the human and leads to a new version, affected-label review and requalification. Clear execution failures route to expression or executor selection; never silently overwrite a frozen policy.

This enlarged decision card is an illustrative form design using synthetic supportiveness examples from the local prototype. It is not real collected user evidence, a prescribed correct labeling rule or an interactive PowerPoint control. The purpose is to show how high-level preferences can be collected through low-friction structured choices. A card presents a clear question, contrastive learning evidence, alternative rules, the current rule, traceable sources, expected effects and affected scope. Users may select an alternative, supply a custom rule, defer, and add comments. All options start unselected. Workbench should render and persist structured agent-generated report content rather than requiring a newly implemented webpage every round. Submission records the person's preference and scope; the Alignment Agent then checks cross-decision consistency and integrates the decision. A rule decision is not automatic item-level approval for propagated labels. Diagnostic decisions can define easy versus hard cases, uncertainty reasons and review actions. Form interaction may be asynchronous; chat supplements the same record.

A rule-level form uses corpus evidence, audit issues and traceable human sources. Staging Train or Test issues may be reviewed here; a direct expression refiner still receives only Train evidence. All options start unselected. Rejection, custom proposal, deferral and unanswered are distinct stored states. Custom rules require text; conditional comments may require a clarified interpretation. Saving a draft is not approval. Explicitly submitting an exact displayed rule patch can approve only that shown scope; an abstract preference such as the displayed A/B/C choices needs integration into exact meaning before executable rule release when interpretation remains. Partial answers can be submitted. Nothing on this static mockup changes actual user preferences.
